text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The midwestern Nigerian oil city of Warri is on the boil again as fresh communal fighting claims one life amidst gun fire and burning of the main market.

- The top Nigerian human rights official, Awwalu Yadudu, accuses European Union of turning United Nations Human Rights Commission into a political forum following censure of Nigeria by the commission at its conference in Geneva.

- Sylvanus Okoli, the retiring managing director of National Oil, Nigeria's largest oil products marketing firm, advocates privatisation of the oil sector to end crises such as the recent fuel shortage.
- Proposed transfer of central bank's retail functions to commercial banks will begin in July, says central bank governor Paul Ogwuma.
- Central bank governor Paul Ogwuma says no going back on plan to liquidate distressed banks which failed to meet a March 31 deadline to recapitalise.
- Cash-strapped Nigeria Airways to receive a 1.2 billion naira lifeline from the federal government.
- Nigerian exports to the United States, mostly crude oil, hit $5.8 billion in 1996, an increase of $1.1 billion or 22.5 percent from the 1995 level.
